- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.2) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (especially < -0.1) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model overreacts to recent spikes; correct by smoothing out immediate post-spike peaks (especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive).
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after strong upward moves — reduce forecast by 5–10% if recent 3–5 day high is followed by negative sentiment.
- Lagged response: model often lags sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 2–3 days, adjust forecast downward to avoid overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early summer (June) — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is positive but price history shows no trend, don’t extrapolate — use 10–15 day moving average as baseline.
